summary.name: Snapback
summary.one_liner: A Mac window manager that saves your full window layout (apps, positions, displays) and restores it with one keystroke.
use_cases: Restore your coding setup after a context switch or call
Reposition apps automatically when plugging or unplugging monitors
Snap windows into halves, thirds or quarters with shortcuts
Arrange all open apps into a preset layout
Keep a consistent workspace across laptop restarts
summary.what_it_does: Snapback saves every open app, window position and display in a named workspace bound to one keystroke, and restores it with another. It adapts when monitors are connected or disconnected, placing windows on the right screen and keeping them off the laptop display. Windows can be snapped to halves, thirds and quarters via shortcuts, or by holding Command and dragging to an edge or corner. A menu bar app provides access to these functions, and the page says every action has a customizable shortcut.
notable: Saves and restores full workspace layout across apps, positions and up to 6 displays with one keystroke
Drag-to-snap with Command key held, plus halves/thirds/quarters shortcuts
Listed in awesome-mac under Window Management as freeware
caveats: Command palette, Spaces, custom layouts and other Pro features require the Pro version at $9.99
Smart launchers and some themes are described under Pro features
